Q: 'Prophet' object has no attribute 'stan_backend' A:

This worked for me on Windows. I had to import StanBackendEnum:

from prophet.models import StanBackendEnum

Q: How to average multiple files across groups A:

I had a go at making some mock data to make it reproducible. Let me know if it fails to reflect your data sufficiently.

# making some names and groups. group sizes are 3, 3 and 2

fnames <- head(paste0("samp_", outer(letters[1:3], 1:3, paste0), ".csv"), -1)
fileid <- do.call("rbind", strsplit(substr(fnames, 6, 7), ""))

# the reference file for making the group averages

meangroups <- data.frame(
  group=fileid[,1], 
  file=fnames, 
  outname=paste(
    "meangroup",
    fileid[,1],
    apply(fileid, 1, function(x) paste(fileid[fileid[,1] == x[1], 2], collapse="-")),
    sep="_"
  )
)
write.csv(meangroups, file="meangroups.csv")

# creating a subdirectory with some randomly generated files, using the predefined names

dir.create("subf")
set.seed(1)
for (i in seq_along(fnames)) {
    write.csv(matrix(sample(0:9, 12, rep=TRUE), nrow=4), file=paste0("subf/", fnames[i]))
}

# remove the recently made objects, we shouldn't need them

rm("fnames", "fileid", "meangroups")

# read in reference file

scang <- read.csv("meangroups.csv", row.names=1)

# i think group_by() works similarly to split here. we could have used tapply() instead
# of lapply(split()), but this makes it a bit more clear what's going on, i think

lapply(split(scang, scang[,1]), 
  function(x) {
      l <- lapply(paste0("subf/", x[,2]), read.csv, row.names=1)
      l.mean <- Reduce("+", l)/length(l)
      write.csv(l.mean, file=paste0(x[1,3], ".csv"))
  })

# chack that it worked

lapply(paste0(unique(scang[,3]), ".csv"), read.csv, row.names=1)

#         V1       V2       V3

# 2 4.000000 6.000000 3.666667

# 4 2.333333 3.000000 9.000000

Q: How to draw an overlay on top of mobile vision barcode scanner? A:

I've just seen your question whilst having to implement a QR code scanner myself.

What worked easily for me was to place everything in a RelativeLayout and simply stack views on top of the SurfaceView. By doing this you can obtain the required overlay effect. 

<RelativeLayout
    xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent"
    tools:context=".view.activity.QRActivity">

<SurfaceView android:id="@+id/surfaceViewBarcode"
             android:layout_width="match_parent"
             android:layout_height="match_parent"/>

<View   android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="match_parent"
        android:alpha="0.5"
        android:background="@android:color/black" />

<TextView android:text="@string/qr_scanText"
          android:gravity="center"
          android:textColor="@android:color/white"
          android:textStyle="bold"
          android:layout_centerInParent="true"
          android:layout_width="match_parent"
          android:layout_height="wrap_content"
          android:layout_alignBottom="@+id/surfaceViewBarcode"
          android:layout_alignParentTop="true"/>

The only inconvenience is the fact that the bar code scanner will pickup the QR code even if it's not placed in the designated area.

After following this thread, I've found out that you have multiple options for achieving the required result. One would be by implementing a custom processor

Another way is by BoxDetector.
